verdict.line: You win this hard before level 6 and in any solo fight, but drag it past mid game and Hallowed Mist plus her fast Needlework recasts pull her back to even.

brief.thesis: Renekton's kit is built to punish the exact window before Gwen has Hallowed Mist online: Fury-empowered W stuns and E gap-closes let him force fights she can't escape. Her passive sustain and Needlework's recast speed at rank 3 (8.5/8s) let her out-poke and disengage once she scales, which is why the 48.3% head-to-head over 553 games sits below the raw lane and solo-kill advantage you actually hold early.

theirWindow.when: once her Hallowed Mist is off cooldown
theirWindow.what: She'll pop it and dare you to walk in; don't chase into the mist blind, since only enemies who enter it can be targeted by her — wait out the 22/21/20/19/18s cooldown or force the trade the moment she uses it elsewhere.

yourWindow.when: levels 1-2, before she has Mist up
yourWindow.what: Take W (Ruthless Predator) first and full commit — auto into W into auto stuns her for 0.75s with no way to disengage since she has no mist yet.

start.why: The 49.4% win rate pick over 528 games — the extra sustain matters because you're initiating most trades and eating some Q (Snip Snip!) true-damage ticks on the way in.

boots.why: 52.5% win rate over 358 games; Gwen's entire kit — passive, Q, R — is magic damage, so the resist is worth more here than Plated Steelcaps' physical mitigation.

core.why: The shield proc lets you tank one Q snip cycle or an R needle and still walk away with the trade during your level 1-8 window.
Armor shred stacks with your empowered E's own armor reduction, letting your Fury-empowered W hit harder as fights extend past the first stun.
45.7% win rate over 46 games on this exact path; the damage-over-time conversion blunts her passive's true-damage-adjacent burst on extended trades.

situational.when: she's landing full Q cones and R needle hits consistently and burst is the problem, not sustain
you're behind and need to survive her Skip 'n Slash on-hit window instead of winning the all-in outright

runes.keystoneWhy: The 35% pick rate page at 48% win rate; the stacking sustain directly offsets her passive's healing off Q snips and R needle hits during the extended trades you're forcing.

summoners.why: 89.8% pick rate at 49% win rate — this is an aggressive, solo-kill-favored matchup before level 6, and Ignite is what turns a good all-in into a kill instead of a reset.

playing.title: All-in at level 1-2
playing.detail: Take W (Ruthless Predator) first if possible — she has no Hallowed Mist yet, so the 0.75s stun into auto is a free trade with no counterplay.

playing.title: Track your Fury bar constantly
playing.detail: Above 50 Fury, W lands a third slash that destroys shields and stuns for 1.5s instead of 0.75s, and Q's damage and heal both increase — bank Fury before committing to a big trade.

playing.title: Never chase into her mist
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist only lets enemies who enter it target her — walking in on cooldown just eats free Q snips and R needle hits for nothing.

playing.title: Use E to shred before W
playing.detail: Empowered Slice and Dice reduces armor on units hit — land it right before your W combo so the follow-up stun ability hits harder.

playing.title: Respect her E reset window
playing.detail: Skip 'n Slash refunds its cooldown on a hit during the attack-speed buff — if she just landed it, expect another dash-away attempt within seconds, not a stand-and-fight.

playing.title: Close the game by mid
playing.detail: Her Needlework recast cooldown drops to 8.5/8s at rank 3 — past that point she can poke and disengage repeatedly, so convert your early lead into towers and objectives instead of playing a long lane.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample numbers are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch; the level-by-level reads on Hallowed Mist timing, Fury thresholds, and trade sequencing are my own tactical analysis, not measured data.
